title: Maccheroni alla Chitarra
subtitle: Square-cut pasta in a slow-cooked lamb and tomato ragu
excerpt: Maccheroni alla chitarra are square spaghetti from Abruzzo, traditionally cut on a guitar-string frame. Here they are paired with a simple lamb and tomato ragu that cooks low and slow until rich and thick.
sourceNotes: Abruzzese tradition pairing guitar-cut pasta with lamb ragu; widely documented in central Italian cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the ragu separately for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight and reheat gently before tossing with fresh pasta.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the ragu and freeze half. It keeps well and improves overnight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The ragu can be made a day ahead and reheated when needed.

content.text: Maccheroni alla chitarra are square-cut spaghetti from the Abruzzo region. Spaghetti works well here if you cannot find the real thing. The lamb ragu needs low, patient heat to turn tender and thick.

items.prepNote: one tin, crushed with your hand

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a medium saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and rosemary. Cook for 1 minute.
Turn the heat up. Add the lamb mince and break it up. Cook for 5 minutes until browned all over.
Pour in the wine if using. Stir and let it bubble away for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and chilli flakes. Season with salt and pepper. Stir well. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce the heat to very low. Cook uncovered for 50 to 60 minutes, stirring occasionally. The ragu should thicken and the oil should separate slightly at the surface.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water, then drain.
Add the pasta to the ragu. Toss well, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen if needed. Serve with grated pecorino.

items.symptom: The ragu is watery after an hour.
items.cause: The heat was too low to reduce the liquid.
items.fix: Increase to a gentle simmer and cook without a lid for a further 15 minutes, stirring often.

items.symptom: The lamb smells gamey and heavy.
items.cause: The mince has a high fat content or was not browned at high enough heat.
items.fix: Make sure the pan is hot before adding the lamb. Brown it in batches if needed so it sears rather than steams.

items.symptom: The pasta has clumped after draining.
items.cause: It sat in the colander too long before being tossed.
items.fix: Move pasta to the ragu immediately after draining and toss straight away.
